questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His research on the migratory patterns of the birds is __run-of-the-mill.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"run-of-the-mill"** means something that is ordinary and not special or exciting in any way. (साधारण)

 
 
• **Example:** The movie was just a **run-of-the-mill **thriller, nothing extraordinary.
 
 
 
• **"Average"** refers to something that is typical, normal, or usual; not special or exceptional. (औसत)
 
 
• **Example:** His performance was **average**, neither outstanding nor poor.
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is '**average**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Absurd** (बेतुका): Something that is ridiculous or unreasonable.

 
 
• **Example:** The idea of flying pigs is completely** absurd.**
 
 
 
• **One in a million** (लाखों में एक): Something that is very special or unique.
 
 
• **Example:** Her talent is truly** one in a million.**
 
 
 
• **Trash** (कचरा): Something that is of very poor quality.
 
 
• **Example:** The novel was so bad it was just** trash.**

• **Impossible** (असंभव): Not able to occur, exist, or be done.

• **Example:** He was hurt by the harsh words of his friend.

questions.question:

Grease someone's palm
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "To bribe someone".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Grease someone's palm"** means to bribe someone in order to gain favor or secure a benefit. (किसी को रिश्वत देना)

 
 
• **Example:** He had to grease the officer's palm to get his work done quickly.
 
 
 
• **"Bribe" **refers to giving someone money or something valuable to persuade them to act dishonestly in your favor. (रिश्वत देना)
 
 
• **Example:** The contractor attempted to bribe the official to approve the faulty construction project.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Grease someone's palm" directly refers to the act of bribing someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To flatter someone **(किसी की चापलूसी करना): To excessively praise or compliment someone, often to gain favor.

 
 
• **Example:** She tried to flatter her boss to get a promotion.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To beat someone **(किसी को मारना): To physically attack or defeat someone.
 
 
• **Example:** The team managed to beat their rivals in the final match.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To abuse someone **(किसी का अपमान करना): To mistreat or speak rudely to someone.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher warned the students not to abuse each other during the debate.

questions.question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His remarks __made the matter worse.__

options.text: Killed two birds with one stone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Added fuel to the fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Added fuel to the fire"** means to make a bad situation worse by doing or saying something that causes more anger or difficulty. (आग में घी डालना)

 
 
• **Example:** Instead of calming the argument, his sarcastic comment only added fuel to the fire.
 
 
 
• The sentence "His remarks made the matter worse" implies that his remarks intensified the problem, which perfectly aligns with the idiom "added fuel to the fire." (आग में घी डालने जैसा काम किया।)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Added fuel to the fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spilled the beans** (राज खोल देना): To reveal a secret or confidential information unintentionally or intentionally.

 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Made a splash** (धूम मचाना): To attract a lot of attention or make a big impression.
 
 
• **Example:** The new fashion designer made a splash with her innovative designs.
 
 
 
• **Killed two birds with one stone** (एक तीर से दो निशाने): To accomplish two objectives with a single action.
 
 
• **Example:** By attending the conference, he killed two birds with one stone: he networked with professionals and learned new skills.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get down to brass tacks
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"get down to brass tacks"** means to start to consider the basic, essential, or important details of a job or task, to focus on the most important details.
 
• **"To become serious about something" -** This phrase generally implies that someone is beginning to focus or concentrate on something, or has decided to take something seriously.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is: *'To become serious about something'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Explanation for other options:
 
 
• **"Get fired from the job" -** This means that someone has been dismissed or let go from their job, typically because of poor performance or some violation of company policy. It doesn't relate to the idiom "get down to brass tacks."
 
• **"Compromise, cooperation between people" -** This indicates a state of agreement reached by adjustment of conflicting or opposing claims, principles, etc., by mutual concessions. It does not encapsulate the meaning of "get down to brass tacks," which pertains to dealing with important details rather than resolving disputes.
 
• **"To be ready" -** This generally means to be prepared for an event or situation. While it may be related in some contexts (you need to be ready before getting down to brass tacks), it doesn't convey the specific idea of dealing with the basic or most important aspects of a situation.
